newsitem.title: FRANCE: French computer firm Bull posts 1996 profit.
newsitem.headline: French computer firm Bull posts 1996 profit.

text.p: French computer maker Bull said on Tuesday that its profits rose in 1996 compared to 1995 and predicted significant profit growth this year.

Bull's profits rose 23 percent to 376 million francs ($65.4 million) last year despite a 612 million franc loss in the first half. The first-half loss was due mostly to one-time charges of 661 million francs at Bull unit Zenith Data Systems, which it merged with Packard Bell NEC in April, 1996.
"Bull looks to the future with confidence and plans to show renewed sales growth in 1997," it said in a statement.
In 1995, Bull reported a full-year profit of 306 million francs after losing a total of 22 billion francs between 1989 and 1994.

The restructuring of its personal computer activities and electronic cards should halt their losses and allow the businesses to be used as levers for higher sales growth, it said. Those businesses generated 4.4 billion francs of turnover in 1996, compared with a restated 1995 turnover of 5.9 billion.
In its systems and services activities, Bull aims for growth outpacing the overall market. Turnover from those activities rose to 19.92 billion francs from 18.61 billion.
"The group in 1997 will pursue its effort to reduce non-wage costs," it said.
Bull also said it may offer a dividend in 1998 based on 1997 results and should pay one in 1999 for the 1998 year, company chairman Jean-Marie Descarpentries said on Tuesday.

"We think we will distribute a dividend in 1999 but in view of our favourable outlook, it could turn out that we will propose a distribution for the 1997 year," Descarpentries told reporters at a news conference. ($ = 5.746 French Francs)
